quote: Faecal S100A12 as a non-invasive marker distinguishing inflammatory bowel disease from irritable bowel syndrome.
summary: Faecal S100A12 distinguishes active IBD, including ulcerative colitis, from IBS and healthy controls with high sensitivity and specificity and reflects inflammatory activity.

quote: More recently, faecal S100A12 has been reported to be an even more accurate faecal marker of inflammation.
summary: Review of stool markers of intestinal inflammation noting faecal S100A12 as an accurate marker and neutrophil-derived DAMP.

quote: Serum and mucosal S100 proteins, calprotectin (S100A8/S100A9) and S100A12, are elevated at diagnosis in children with inflammatory bowel disease.
summary: Serum and mucosal S100A12 are increased in paediatric IBD at diagnosis and indicate disease activity.

quote: S100A12 is a novel molecular marker differentiating systemic-onset juvenile idiopathic arthritis from other causes of fever of unknown origin.
summary: Serum S100A12 is a diagnostic marker for systemic-onset JIA and FMF; the study does not involve UC.

quote: S100A12 and MRP8/14 provoked up-regulation of adhesion molecules and chemokines on human intestinal microvascular endothelial cells (HIMECs) isolated from normal colonic tissue.
summary: S100A12 is released from inflamed IBD tissue and, applied to colonic endothelial cells, induces adhesion molecules and chemokines, promoting inflammation.
